known_facts_book1: An orphan girl who lives on the great gray Kansas prairies with her Uncle Henry, a farmer, and his wife Aunt Em.
A cyclone carries her, her dog Toto, and the whole farmhouse through the air and sets the house down in the Land of Oz.
Her falling house lands on the Wicked Witch of the East and kills her, freeing the Munchkins.
Takes the dead Witch of the East's Silver Shoes from the table and wears them for the rest of the book.
Is greeted as a Sorceress by the Munchkins and kissed on the forehead by the Witch of the North, whose kiss leaves a protecting mark.
Sets out along the road of yellow brick for the Emerald City to ask the Great Oz to send her back to Kansas.
Lifts the Scarecrow off his pole, oils the Tin Woodman's rusted joints, and gains the Cowardly Lion as a travelling companion.
Is carried by the Winged Monkeys and made the Wicked Witch of the West's captive slave in the kitchen of her castle.
Melts the Wicked Witch of the West by throwing a bucket of water over her in a fit of anger.
Uses the Golden Cap to summon the Winged Monkeys and be carried back to the Emerald City.
Discovers that Oz is only a little old humbug hiding behind a screen, not a real wizard.
Misses the Wizard's balloon home because Toto jumps from her arms to chase a kitten and the ropes break before she can climb in.
Journeys south to the Quadling country to ask Glinda for help, crossing the hill of the Hammer-Heads.
Learns from Glinda that the Silver Shoes can carry her anywhere in three steps, and uses them to return to Kansas.
Loses the Silver Shoes during the flight across the desert, so they are gone forever when she lands.
Runs across the Kansas prairie into Aunt Em's arms, home again.

known_relations_book1.Toto: Her little black dog, her one companion from Kansas, carried through every adventure.
known_relations_book1.Scarecrow: The first companion she rescues; he seeks brains and becomes her devoted friend.
known_relations_book1.Tin Woodman: Companion she frees by oiling his joints; he seeks a heart.
known_relations_book1.Cowardly Lion: Companion who joins after failing to frighten her; he seeks courage.
known_relations_book1.Wicked Witch: The Witch of the West, her captor and enemy, whom she accidentally melts with water.
known_relations_book1.Wizard: The humbug she journeys to see; he cannot magically send her home and departs by balloon without her.
known_relations_book1.Glinda: The Good Witch of the South who finally tells her how the Silver Shoes can carry her home.
known_relations_book1.Aunt Em: Her aunt and guardian in Kansas, whom she longs to return to throughout.
known_relations_book1.Uncle Henry: Her uncle, the Kansas farmer she lives with.

known_facts_book1: Dorothy's little black dog with long silky hair and small black eyes that twinkle merrily.
The one thing that makes Dorothy laugh and keeps her from growing as gray as the Kansas prairie.
Falls through the trap-door of the farmhouse during the cyclone but is caught and pulled back by Dorothy.
Travels the whole journey with Dorothy, usually carried or running at her heels.
Is snatched up by a Winged Monkey and carried along when the band seizes the travellers for the Wicked Witch.
Bites the Cowardly Lion's nose in fun when they first meet and is never harmed by him.
Jumps away in alarm at the Lion's roar and tips over the screen that hides the Wizard, accidentally exposing him.
Runs into the crowd to bark at a kitten just as the Wizard's balloon is leaving, which is why Dorothy is left behind.
Does not speak at any point in the book.

known_relations_book1.Dorothy: His mistress; the two are inseparable from Kansas to Oz and back.
known_relations_book1.Cowardly Lion: Sleeps beside the Lion and barks at him without ever being eaten.
